# Recorded examples

The examples on this page run in CI against these recordings from the live bridge, replayed by a stand-in bridge that answers only a call the recording fits:

- [`proteins_read_human.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLibRust/blob/main/tests/fixtures/proteins_read_human.json)

# References

- [doi:10.1038/75556](https://doi.org/10.1038/75556): The Gene Ontology and its three aspects (Ashburner et al. 2000, Nature Genetics)
- [doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1010](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae1010): UniProt, the source of the XML's organism, taxonomy, GO and Ensembl cross-references (UniProt Consortium 2025, NAR)
- [doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1239](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkaf1239): Ensembl, whose transcript and gene ids the ensembl\_genes table carries (Ensembl 2026, NAR)

# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- result.tables (go\_terms, ensembl\_genes) is not validated by tools/check\_verbs.py, which checks only 'columns' and 'bulk'. On 2026-10-21 proteins\_read\_human.json matched both lists exactly, but nothing fails if one drifts: the pyMzLib tests read only some of the columns.
- No --out TSV mode yet (BULK.md §2 mentions one): multi-table output is JSON only, since three tables would need three files.
- proteins\_read\_filtered.json (a one-path read filtered by accession) is used only by the pyMzLib tests. The doctest replay bridge cannot answer a one-path proteins read: it treats any recording with files\[\] and no top-level path as bulk, and this verb always returns files\[\]. Filtered and unfiltered reads are told apart (pyMzLib \#72); the guide's filtered recording proteins\_read\_accessions.json comes through conftest REPLAY\_EXTRA, not through this spec's examples.
